next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST, also tracked as FIN7: a financially motivated group that moved from card theft to ransomware
next.in_short: GOLD LOCUST is a catalogue name for a group also tracked as FIN7 and Carbanak. SentinelOne calls it financially motivated and says it moved into ransomware in 2020. Reports describe mailed USB drives, custom malware and tools sold to…

sentences.t: The catalogue lists GOLD LOCUST under the aliases Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider, FIN7 and Silicon, and names Carbanak as its tool.
SentinelOne describes FIN7 as an elusive, persistent and financially motivated group with origins in Russia.
Morphisec Labs says it has tracked FIN7, which it also calls the Carbanak Group, for several years.
In a 2017 post, FireEye said FIN7 kept up attacks on the restaurant, hospitality and financial services sectors.
The FBI warned in 2020 that FIN7 mailed packages to retail, restaurant and hotel businesses.
BleepingComputer reports that in 2018 the group hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor to steal payment card information.
SentinelOne lists hospitality, energy, finance, high-tech and retail among the industries that suffered losses.
Per the FBI alert, the group posted USB drives that act as keyboards. They launch commands that fetch GRIFFON malware. One lure was a gift card offer.
Malpedia describes GRIFFON as a lightweight JavaScript implant with no persistence. It receives modules to run in memory and sends results to its servers.
FireEye reported that in April 2017 FIN7 shifted to running JavaScript through wscript.exe. It also hid shortcut files in its phishing lures.
Morphisec describes a chain that starts with a phishing invoice and runs script stages in memory. A final script then loads Carbanak.

The Hacker News, citing NCC Group, reports Carbanak delivered through compromised websites that host fake installers for business software such as HubSpot, Veeam and Xero. The report says FIN7 has used Carbanak.
SentinelOne attributes automated SQL injection intrusions to FIN7 with medium confidence. It says they ran through a platform called Checkmarks.

SentinelOne says that from 2020 the group shifted to ransomware, affiliating with groups such as REvil and Conti. It also says the group launched its own services under the names Darkside and then BlackMatter.
S2W also says Darkside, known to be used by the FIN7 group, was rebranded as BlackMatter.
Malwarebytes attributes a late-June malspam campaign to FIN7, described in an August 2022 post. It dropped a rewritten JSSLoader and a second .NET payload.
SentinelOne assesses with high confidence that several forum sellers of antivirus-killer tools belong to the FIN7 cluster. It says the group began developing its AvNeutralizer tool in April 2022.
SentinelOne says it cannot conclusively tell whether LockBit intrusions that used AvNeutralizer were run by FIN7. It reports no direct evidence linking them to the group.
A November 2022 SentinelLABS report described custom EDR evasion tools used in Black Basta attacks as tied to FIN7.
Treat unexpected USB drives and mailed gift offers as hostile, and do not plug them into work machines.
Download business software only from the vendor's own site, not from links in emails or on third-party pages.
